experiment: BUG-01: (A) foreground trusted browser receipts report delivery=background; (B) per-call CDP session accumulation
status: pre-registered before any measured trial of part A or part B; not edited after measured runs start (deviations go to README 'Deviations')

knowledge_before_registration.source_reading: Part A: libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/action_record.rs actual_delivery_from_legacy returns ActualDelivery::Background for browser_click/browser_pointer/browser_type before any producer or request field is consulted; browser/tools.rs BrowserClickTool emits delivery_mode=foreground on its foreground trusted branch; browser/pointer.rs success_json emits no delivery_mode. Part B: browser/engine.rs attach() sends Target.attachToTarget on every revalidate_for_mutation, snapshot_tab, snapshot_tab_semantic, capture and ref-resolution path; the only Target.detachFromTarget calls detach OOPIF child sessions, never the per-call tab session.
knowledge_before_registration.unit_red_run: The new test foreground_trusted_browser_input_receipt_does_not_claim_background_delivery was compiled and run once at main + test (before this file was committed) to check it fails for the stated reason: it failed with public receipt {route: trusted_input, delivery.mode: background}. The guard test background_browser_receipts_keep_background_delivery passed. This is UNIT evidence, re-recorded after the test commit.
knowledge_before_registration.no_real_trials_yet: No REAL or BENCHMARK trial of this lane has run. Wave-0 numbers (R2-02 session-age drift, R2-06 receipts) motivate the hypotheses and are never compared with this lane's numbers.

governing_contract_text.macos_background_input_v1_plan_md: libs/cua-driver/docs/macos-background-input-v1-plan.md: 'Keep successful action outputs on the current `ActionResult` contract: ... `delivery.mode` reports what actually occurred;'
governing_contract_text.action_record_rs_doc: ActualDelivery: 'The delivery mode actually used by the actuator. `Unknown` means an attempt was made but the actuator could not determine whether it delivered in the requested mode.' from_legacy: 'it reports `Unknown` rather than copying a requested delivery mode when the old payload did not prove what actually happened.' structured_delivery_mode: 'Prefer an explicit producer-emitted mode when one exists.'
governing_contract_text.browser_delivery_mode_schema: browser/tools.rs schema_delivery_mode: 'background (default) refuses trusted input where it would activate the browser window (Linux Chromium). foreground accepts that activation, for a browser whose window nobody else is using (for example inside a sandbox).'
governing_contract_text.browser_plan_cdp_sessions: libs/cua-driver/docs/browser-tool-implementation-plan.md: 'Session cleanup detaches its CDP sessions without closing a socket still used by another Cua session.' and risk table: 'Cross-session CDP delivery | Flat mode and one CDP session ID per Cua session/tab'.

part_A.hypothesis: HA: successful foreground trusted browser_click receipts report delivery.mode=background on the baseline because actual_delivery_from_legacy hard-codes Background for browser tools, although the executed branch is the foreground one (trusted background is refused before dispatch on Linux Chromium).

unit.failing_test: cua-driver-core browser::v2_tests::foreground_trusted_browser_input_receipt_does_not_claim_background_delivery (mock CDP, platform with the Linux trusted-background limitation): drives BrowserClickTool {ref, delivery_mode: foreground} and BrowserPointerTool {action: double_click, delivery_mode: foreground}, builds the receipt exactly as the dispatch seam does (from_legacy -> public_result) and asserts route trusted_input and delivery.mode != background (expected foreground). Expected: FAIL at main+test, PASS at fix.
unit.guard_test: browser::v2_tests::background_browser_receipts_keep_background_delivery: dom_event click and dom_event pointer with a stray delivery_mode=foreground request stay background; trusted background click is refused with no delivery; browser_type with a stray delivery_mode=foreground stays background. Expected: PASS at main+test and at fix.

real.fixture: jev-use fixture_server.py PAGE served by a probe subclass that appends a capture-phase listener (sendBeacon -> POST /events journal: pointer/mouse/click/focus/input/submit with isTrusted, document.hasFocus(), visibilityState) and journals POST /submit server-side before delegating to the unmodified handler (as R2-06). Per-trial POST /reset and fresh browser_navigate. Agent-cursor feedback at the Driver default (as R2-06).

arms.T: browser_type {ref: textbox 'verification value', text: per-trial token, replace: true} then browser_click {ref: Submit, delivery_mode: 'foreground'} (default input_route=trusted). Forced path = R2-06 arm T: CDP Input.dispatchMouseEvent on the foreground branch. n=20.
arms.D: browser_type as in T, then browser_click {ref: Submit, input_route: 'dom_event'} (no delivery_mode). n=20.
arms.Y: browser_type {ref: textbox, text: per-trial token, replace: true} only; no click. n=20.
arms.N_bg: control: browser_type then browser_click {ref: Submit} with default background delivery (trusted) -> expected refused (browser_input_trust_unavailable), no delivery field, no page pointer events, /state null. n=5.
arms.N_domfg: control: browser_type then browser_click {ref: Submit, input_route: 'dom_event', delivery_mode: 'foreground'} -> expected route dom and delivery background on BOTH binaries (the request alone is not proof; a synthetic DOM click is full-background). n=5.

real.blocks: Per binary: 7 blocks x 10 trials, each block a fresh Driver MCP process + fresh isolated_new browser. Blocks 1-6 hold the 60 T/D/Y trials in the rotating patterns TDYYDTDYTY / DYTTYDYTDT / YTDDTYTDYD (each pattern twice; 20 per arm). Block 7 holds N_bg/N_domfg alternating (5+5). Baseline run first (after this file is committed), fix run after the fix commit; same harness, plan and environment. Both runs hold quiet-lane.lock SHARED.
real.per_trial_records: full MCP structuredContent receipts for browser_type and browser_click; page journal; X11 focus pre/post (xdotool getactivewindow, _NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW) and browser window id; fixture /state immediate read and bounded re-reads every 50 ms up to 3000 ms; loadavg.

oracles.page_trusted_foreground: T trial: page journal shows pointerdown and click on button{Submit} with isTrusted=true, document.hasFocus()=true and visibilityState=visible at pointerdown, and X11 active window == the browser window before and after the click.
oracles.target_effect: fixture /state submitted == per-trial token (T, D, N_domfg) or stays null (Y, N_bg); fixture POST /submit journal count.
oracles.type_effect: page journal input event(s) with value_len == len(token) (Y and every T/D/N trial).

real.receipt_fields_compared: effect, route, delivery.mode, delivery.delivered_count, evidence, escalation, error per tool call. summary is prose and is compared only after replacing numbers with '#'.

gates.CONFIRMED_BUG: ALL of: (1) baseline reports delivery.mode=background on >=1 accepted T trial whose page oracle shows trusted foreground; (2) the failing test fails at main+test and passes at the fix; (3) with the fix, T reports foreground on every accepted T trial and D, Y, N_domfg report background, N_bg has no delivery; (4) no other compared receipt field changes between baseline and fix in any arm, and no contract/golden test changes outcome or expectation.

part_B.hypothesis: HB: each browser tool call attaches a CDP session (Target.attachToTarget) without a matching detach, so live sessions and per-call CDP event volume grow linearly with calls in one Driver session.
part_B.instrumentation: Measurement-only, env-gated, default-off: CUA_DRIVER_EXP_CDP_COUNTER_FILE (unset = no file, no work). New cua-driver-core/src/browser/cdp_counters.rs; hooks in cdp_ws.rs (command sent/acknowledged, every parsed frame) and one call at the end of the tool dispatch seam. One JSONL line per completed tool call: attach/detach commands sent and acknowledged, attachedToTarget/detachedFromTarget events, live session set size, sessions seen, replies/events cumulative and per-call delta, frames and events per session id since the previous line. Unit tests in the module; default-off smoke = stock browser-smoke.sh with the instrumented binary and the variable unset (rc 0, no counter file anywhere in the retained session dir).
part_B.page: jev-use PAGE with one injected <button type="button" id="bug01-noop">No-op</button> (no handler, no form) inside <main>; served by the jev-use fixture server subclass.
part_B.session_setup: MCP initialize -> set_agent_cursor_enabled {enabled: false} (both arms; removes the ~1.5 s awaited glide so a ms-scale slope is measurable) -> browser_prepare {allow_launch, isolated_new} -> list_windows poll -> get_browser_state {pid, window_id} -> browser_navigate fixture. Setup calls are not in the measured series.
part_B.call_sequence: call k (0-based): even k -> get_browser_state {snapshot_format: semantic_v2}; odd k -> browser_click {ref: the No-op ref from the latest snapshot, input_route: dom_event}.

arms.L: long session: one Driver + browser, calls k=0..299 (300 calls).
arms.C: fresh-session control: 30 blocks x 10 calls (k=0..9), each block a fresh Driver + browser; series index s = 10*block + k (0..299).

part_B.navigation_probe: secondary, pre-registered: in each L session a browser_navigate reload of the fixture before k=0, before k=100, before k=200 and after k=299 (4 probes, not in the series; the next call after a probe is always a snapshot). In C, each block's setup browser_navigate is the fresh-session probe (30 per C series). Metric: events received during the navigate call vs live sessions at that moment.
part_B.rss: Every 25 calls in L (k=0,25,...,300) and at the start and end of each C block: VmRSS and Pss (smaps_rollup) summed over the Chrome process tree rooted at this lane's browser_prepare pid, plus the renderer processes separately (read-only /proc).
part_B.order_and_lock: One isolated-session invocation: L1 C1 C2 L2 L3 C3 (ABBA at series level), holding quiet-lane.lock EXCLUSIVE for the whole run. loadavg recorded per call and per block. Every call kept; failures stay in the denominator.
part_B.pilot: Up to 2 short plumbing pilots before the measured run (<=1 long session of <=20 calls and <=1 control block), excluded from every number and retained under raw/pilot/.

metrics.M1: cumulative attach_sent - detach_sent and live_sessions vs k (L) and vs s (C).
metrics.M2: per-call events_delta (CDP events received during the call) vs k, excluding navigation probes.
metrics.M3: per-call latency (client-side MCP call_tool elapsed ms) vs k, with a call-type intercept (snapshot vs click).

part_B.statistics: OLS slope per session (M3 with a call-type dummy); pooled slope = mean of the 3 per-session slopes; 95% CI by seeded moving-block bootstrap within each session (block 25 calls, 10000 resamples, seed 20261002). C slopes the same way over s and over within-block k. Effect size = L latency slope in ms per 100 calls with CI, and L minus C (series index) with CI from independent resampling of both arms.

gates.CONFIRMED: M1 pooled slope (attach-minus-detach or live_sessions) > 0 with CI excluding 0 AND M2 pooled slope > 0 with CI excluding 0. Effect size = M3 latency slope (ms/100 calls) with CI.
gates.REFUTED: M1 and M2 both flat (CI includes 0).
gates.ACCUMULATION_ONLY: pre-registered intermediate: M1 slope > 0 (CI excludes 0) but M2 flat on this no-op workload; reported with M3, M4 and the navigation probe M5, which decides whether accumulated sessions amplify events when the page changes.
gates.if_confirmed_or_accumulation: add a minimal failing repro (ignored unit test over mock CDP asserting attach - detach <= 1 per Cua session/tab, or a repro script); the fix is out of scope and is routed to the upstream browser-timing owner trycua/cua 4052 (plain text).
gates.drift_statement: State whether R2-01/R2-02-style single-session runs (navigation per trial) carry a drift term, from M3 and M5.
